description:
Alexstra is a multidisciplinary team from Alexandria driven by technology, innovation, and space exploration. We aim to turn complex challenges into practical, creative solutions.

Our goal is simple: build something meaningful, innovative, and impactful together.
summary: ARES is a browser game that teaches how to read a map of Mars in order to stay alive on it. You are an astronaut on foot in Jezero Crater with a limited oxygen tank. A stranded companion, ARES, needs three pieces of its ship. Every tile of the board is built from real NASA data: slope from the HiRISE 1 m terrain model, ground firmness from THEMIS night-time infrared, and the surface image from the HiRISE orthomosaic. An A* planner with a cost made from slope and ground softness draws the safest walk; the player can follow it or explore and pay for it in oxygen and risk. The game shows why this matters: at Perseverance's landing site the planned walk uses 15% less oxygen than the shortest one, crosses 8 dangerous tiles instead of 39, and cuts the chance of an accident from 68% to 18%. We checked the map against the real rover: Perseverance's own track stays on the ground our map calls safe. The game runs in 2D and 3D, in any browser, with nothing to install.
details:
What it does. ARES turns a 1.6 km × 1.52 km window of Jezero Crater, centred on Perseverance's landing site (18.4447° N, 77.4508° E), into a board of 40 × 40 tiles of 40 m each. The player walks tile by tile to recover three ship pieces and return before the oxygen runs out. Steep tiles and soft sand cost more oxygen; tiles steeper than 15° cannot be crossed; dangerous tiles carry a chance of an accident. Five map layers can be switched at any time: the game art, the real HiRISE photo, height, slope and night heat. A key switches between the 2D map and a 3D view of the same terrain, with third-person and first-person cameras. At the wreck, a ship computer holds every NASA image of the site, the four orbital maps and ground data measured live from the layers. The game has a main menu with settings and works on phones and tablets with touch controls.

How it works.

  • Data pipeline (Python, tools/): streams only the needed window of the HiRISE DTM by HTTP range requests, computes slope, reads THEMIS and HiRISE map tiles from NASA Mars Trek, and reads the Mars 2020 rover's waypoints, track and Navcam photos. Nothing is invented: every tile value comes from these products.
  • Route planner (game/astar.js): A* on the tile grid. Cost of a step = 40 m × (1 + 2.5 × (slope / 15°)² + 0.6 × softness), impassable above 15°. The tour over the three pieces is chosen by trying every order.
  • ARES, the companion (game/ares.js): not a language model. Directions are read off the real A* path; oxygen, slope and risk are computed from the data; other questions are answered by search over a written knowledge base about the NASA data and the mission, and each answer names its source. Unknown questions are refused instead of guessed.
  • Landing sites: besides Perseverance's site, the game offers three sites on ground no rover has reached (more than 200 m from the whole traverse), screened for slope, firmness and room like a real landing site.
  • Game (HTML, JavaScript, Canvas 2D, three.js for 3D). No build step, no server, no account.

Validation against the real rover. Perseverance drove across this same board (sols 14–386). On our map its tiles average 4.2° of slope against 6.1° for the whole board; 5.4% of its tiles are steeper than 10° against 10.1%; none of its 93 tiles is over our 15° limit; and our terrain heights match the rover's own recorded elevations to ±0.08 m at 85 stops. The real mission chose the same kind of ground our planner chooses.

Benefits and impact. Future crews will walk on Mars with a fixed amount of air. The shortest line on a map is often not the cheapest or the safest. ARES makes that visible and playable for children and students, from about age 10, and for the public: it teaches slope, thermal inertia and path planning through real mission data, and shows in numbers what a good route saves. The same method works for any place on Mars that has a terrain model.

What is not data (stated openly in the game and README). The story, the oxygen tank size, the accident probabilities, the 15° limit and the cost weights are our design choices. THEMIS is used as a relative measure inside this window, not as a calibrated temperature.

Tools and languages. JavaScript (ES modules), HTML/CSS, Canvas 2D, WebGL through three.js r160, Web Audio; Python with NumPy, SciPy and Pillow for the data tools; Git and GitHub Pages for hosting.

Links. Play: https://3zz2004.github.io/ARES-/ · Source code: https://github.com/3zz2004/ARES- · Project description (PDF): https://3zz2004.github.io/ARES-/demo/ARES_Project_Description.pdf

Use of AI (stated openly). AI tools were used to build what the team designed.

  • The team's own work: the idea and the design (a survival walk on real Mars data with a companion who reads the data for you; the rules, the levels, the oxygen, the landing sites); the decisions (e.g. a radiation layer was removed because no real data backed it; ARES may answer only from NASA data and must name his source; the route had to be checked against the real rover); direction, art direction and testing of every build.
  • Code: written with an AI coding assistant (Claude, by Anthropic) to the team's design, then tested and corrected by the team build by build. Stated in the README, in AI_DISCLOSURE.md, and in a comment and metadata tag in the game's HTML.
  • Images: the characters, ground textures, rocks and objects were generated with ChatGPT (OpenAI) image generation, to the team's art direction, then cut and placed by our own code. Every one is marked: a visible "AI-GENERATED ART" label on the game screen and in the opening cinematic, a banner on every source sheet in art_src/, and a text note in each PNG's metadata. No generated image contains NASA logos, flags or mission identifiers.
  • Not AI: all terrain, slope, thermal, rover-track and photo data is NASA/USGS data; no data was generated or changed by AI. No AI model runs inside the game: ARES answers with computation and search. The opening music is a human-made track from Pixabay; all other sound is synthesised by code.
  • Demo video: the pictures are rendered by code from the project's real map layers and routes and its AI-generated character art, and carry an "AI-generated visuals" label. The narration is an AI voice (ElevenLabs).
dataRefs: HiRISE DTM of Jezero Crater, 1 m/pixel (MRO HiRISE; USGS Astrogeology, Mars 2020 TRN) - slope, elevation, 3D terrain
HiRISE orthomosaic of Jezero, 25 cm/pixel, via NASA Mars Trek - PHOTO layer and board colours
THEMIS Night IR controlled mosaic, 100 m/pixel (Mars Odyssey), via NASA Mars Trek - ground softness and HEAT layer
Mars 2020 Perseverance waypoints and traverse - rover path and validation
Mars 2020 raw images, Navcam - real photos at each ship piece
